titolo: What I Used to Call a “Starter”
copy:
This photo is from my own kitchen. This wasn't a party, a holiday, or a cheat day. This was Tuesday.
⠀
I never thought of myself as someone with a "diet problem." I just liked meat, and I could put away an amount that, looking back, should've told me something was off. Nobody in my house questioned it because I'd always eaten like this — big guy, big appetite, that's just who I was. Until I was 46, stepping on a scale I'd been avoiding for a year, seeing a number I'd never let myself imagine.
⠀
My brother-in-law had lost a serious amount of weight the year before and I'd chalked it up to him "finally eating right." Turned out that wasn't the whole story. He told me over a family dinner — the same kind of dinner where I was probably eating like this photo — that his testosterone had been quietly tanking for years, and it wasn't until he addressed that directly that the weight actually started coming off and staying off. He'd started TStrive. Natural ingredients, Tongkat Ali, Tribulus, Zinc, three capsules before bed, nothing complicated. Said it didn't ask him to stop loving food. It just fixed the part of his body that was working against him no matter how much he ate or didn't eat.
⠀
I started that same week, still skeptical, still eating the way I always had at first.
⠀
Week 4: Down 8 lbs, without cutting a single meal I actually cared about.
⠀
Month 2: Down 20 lbs. Started noticing I felt full on portions I used to consider a "starter."
⠀
Month 3: Down 32 lbs. Went back and looked at this exact photo and genuinely didn't recognize how much food that was.
⠀
Month 5: Down 44 lbs. I still eat meat. I still love a good cut. I just don't eat like this photo anymore — and I don't need to, to feel satisfied.
⠀
I kept the picture. It's the best "before" I've got, even though there's not a single person in it.
